title: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulation of Au(001) film growth
action: Implement a kMC simulator on a 160×160×4 fcc(001) lattice with periodic boundaries. For energetic deposition, use the MD-derived push-out probability P_push = 1 − 0.2·n_b·ρ/a_u (with a_u=0.5a₀) and redistribution radius R_D = 2.83 a_u. For conventional deposition, use downward funnelling. Hopping rate h = ν exp(−E_B/kT) with ν = 0.5×10¹² Hz. Compute barriers E_B via the Breeman et al. local-environment model and the Au EAM potential using a three-dimensional Newton‑Raphson saddle-point search. Deposit at 0.05 ML/s at substrate temperatures 100, 300, 400, and 450 K. Save surface configurations at 0.2 ML and at intervals up to 5 ML.
description: Required simulation stage that produces the raw atomistic surfaces needed for subsequent analysis steps.

title: Compute island size distribution and monomer fraction after 0.2 ML deposition
action: From the saved surface configurations at 0.2 ML, extract the island size distribution (coverage per island size), compute the monomer fraction and the stable-island count for each temperature and deposition type (energetic and conventional). Write the results to step_01_island_stats.json.
description: Island statistics after 0.2 ML deposition for energetic and conventional deposition at the four temperatures.
output_schema: JSON object with key 'temperatures' containing an array of objects. Each object: { 'temperature': float (K), 'deposition_type': 'energetic'|'conventional', 'island_size_distribution': [ { 'size': int, 'coverage': float (ML) } ], 'monomer_fraction': float, 'stable_island_count': int }

title: Compute Bragg intensity and surface roughness up to 5 ML coverage
action: From the saved surface configurations at multiple coverages (up to 5 ML), compute the kinematic Bragg intensity and RMS surface roughness as functions of coverage for each temperature and deposition type. Write the results to step_02_bragg_roughness.json.
description: Bragg intensity and roughness evolution up to 5 ML for all conditions.
output_schema: JSON object with key 'temperatures' containing an array of objects. Each object: { 'temperature': float (K), 'deposition_type': 'energetic'|'conventional', 'coverage': [float (ML)], 'bragg_intensity': [float], 'roughness': [float] }
